### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05b28c199b7408da7ca4bc3988635fa9342cd6de` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6560b87021b940c8463f6424743c5db541508571` — the merge of head `58d0be84ffd522783c97313570a02e0971989ee9` into base `05b28c199b7408da7ca4bc3988635fa9342cd6de`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6560b87021b940c8463f6424743c5db541508571 && git checkout 6560b87021b940c8463f6424743c5db541508571
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 05b28c199b7408da7ca4bc3988635fa9342cd6de 58d0be84ffd522783c97313570a02e0971989ee9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 05b28c199b7408da7ca4bc3988635fa9342cd6de && git merge --no-ff 58d0be84ffd522783c97313570a02e0971989ee9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05b28c199b7408da7ca4bc3988635fa9342cd6de
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 05b28c199b7408da7ca4bc3988635fa9342cd6de` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `58d0be84ffd522783c97313570a02e0971989ee9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-format-refusal.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-format-warning.test.ts + packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/branding.manifest.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/company.manifest.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/mail.manifest.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/runtime-config-plugin.ts, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md, and the two prose faces .changeset/24882-settings-format-refusal.md and .changeset/24882-settings-format-warning.md (judged sentence by sentence in ①)

Inputs: card #24882 (body and all nine comments), PR #25022 (body, file list, the net diff against main at the head above, five paths), and the check-runs on that head. Read-only: the cited code was read with git show at the head and at origin/main; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.

- **J1 — the save door narrows (right).** `validatePatch` now pushes one `FieldError` for a non-empty string value that misses the format its specifier type declares, with `code` from the shared verdict (`invalid_email` / `invalid_url` / `invalid_phone`, and `invalid_format` for `color`), `message` of the form `LABEL must be EXPECTED.`, `label`, and `constraint: { type }`, then `continue`s; `SettingsValidationError` is thrown before any write, and `settings-routes.ts` maps it to `400` `SETTINGS_VALIDATION` with the array in `error.details.fields`. So `PUT /api/settings/:namespace` and `setMany` refuse what they answered `200` to on main. Reach, re-derived at the head over every manifest in the tree: `branding.accent_color` (color), `branding.logo_url` (url), `company.website` (url), `company.primary_contact_email` (email) and `mail.from_email` (email, required). The other `type: 'url'` spellings in the tree (`settings-service-plugin.ts`, `datasource-admin-plugin.ts`, platform-objects nav) are Setup navigation items, not specifiers; no shipped manifest authors a `phone` specifier (`company.phone` is `text`). The PR and the note list exactly these five keys.
- **J2 — family order kept (right).** The format branch is the last branch of the specifier loop in `validatePatch` and the last check in `effectiveEnvOverride`, after required, options, pattern, valueDomain and bounds on the one door and options, pattern, valueDomain and bounds on the other. Every earlier branch `continue`s or returns once it has spoken, so a value that also breaks another declared constraint is refused for that one, and the errors a patch that was already refused on main carries are unchanged. The pattern branch's `invalid_format` carries `constraint.pattern`; the colour branch's carries `constraint.type`, so the two are distinguishable without parsing the sentence.
- **J3 — stored rows and the TOUCH gate (right).** `validatePatch` returns early on an all-null patch and judges a specifier only when the patch names its key or a key its `visible` predicate reads, so a row stored before this check is still served by `get`, `getNamespace` and the GET route and does not block a save of the namespace's other keys; it is refused only by a patch that writes it, or by a save of a key its `visible` reads. The pin file holds all three legs per type, the reset leg and the `visible`-TOUCH leg on a synthetic key; no shipped format-typed key declares `visible`.
- **J4 — the env door narrows (right).** A malformed `OS_*` override is now handed to `reportRejectedEnvOverride` and `effectiveEnvOverride` returns `null`, so the override contributes nothing, locks nothing, and the key resolves from the stored value, else the manifest default, with that layer reported as the source. The line is `error`, deduped per `ENVVAR=value` in memory for the life of the service, and arrives at boot because `auditEnvOverrides` walks format-typed keys by type (`DECLARED_VALUE_FORMATS.has(declaredTypeOf(...))`, unchanged from PR #25001), else on the first read. `envKeyOf` spells the variable `OS_` plus namespace and key upper-cased, as the pins assume.
- **J5 — no echo on either refusal path (right).** Save door: `message` interpolates only `label` (manifest text) and `miss.expected` (a per-type constant naming no part of the value); no `value` member and no `Received` fragment is attached; `SettingsValidationError.message` concatenates field and message only, and the route forwards `err.message` and `fields` and nothing else. Env door: with `shape` set the reporter's `rejected` fragment is `The rejected value is a string of N characters; it is not printed.` for every key, encrypted or not; `what`, `detail` and `fix` are built from `formatMiss.type` and `formatMiss.expected` only; the value appears solely in the in-memory `dedupeAt` key. The other families' lines are untouched and still print a non-secret value, which is main's behaviour and outside this card. Pinned at both doors, including a secret-bearing key and fragment checks.
- **J6 — wire shape stays inside the published schema (right).** `invalid_email`, `invalid_url`, `invalid_phone` and `invalid_format` are members of the closed `FieldErrorCode` catalog in `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`; `FieldError.constraint` is an open record, so `{ type: 'url' }` parses (the pins run `FieldErrorSchema.safeParse` on the entry), and `value` is optional. `constraint.type` is a new key on this wire, spelled by the declaring manifest property as `{ pattern }`, `{ valueDomain }`, `{ visible }` and `{ allowed }` are. No response member is added and no spec file changes.
- **J7 — the warning surface is removed (right).** The save door's `formatMisses` list and post-accept `warn` loop, the env door's `reportEnvFormatMiss` reporter and its `reportedEnvFormatMisses` set are deleted; no `warn` line remains on either door for this family. Log lines are not a contract surface; the new note states the change.
- **J8 — no export changes (right).** The diff adds, removes or re-types no exported declaration in `settings-service.ts`; `reportRejectedEnvOverride`'s optional `shape` fragment is on a private method. Nothing outside `service-settings` changes.
- **J9 — grammars unchanged (right), one precision.** The four regexes in `DECLARED_VALUE_FORMATS` are byte-identical to main; only the doc comment changes. The `url` grammar admits `scheme://`, a root-relative `/path`, `data:` and `blob:`; a document-relative spelling (no leading slash) and a scheme without `//` are refused as `invalid_url`. The shipped readers sit inside the grammar (the manifest's example is `https://…/logo.svg`; storage hands back a root-relative path). The "absolute or relative URL" wording lives on `RuntimeConfigPlugin.logoUrl` in `runtime-config-plugin.ts`, the host-level `OS_LOGO_URL` reader, which this door does not judge (the PR says so).
- **J10 — the pin file (right).** `settings-format-warning.test.ts` is deleted and `settings-format-refusal.test.ts` keeps every pin of it that is still true (the other shapes each grammar admits, empty and blank, the secret-bearing key on both doors, precedence on both doors, a well-formed value per type) and adds the refusal pins, the batch pin, the stored-row pins, the reset pin and the `visible`-TOUCH pin. The save door is driven through the real route with status starting at 0; the env door through `get`, `getNamespace`, the GET route and the PUT lock. The deleted "a well-formed override draws no warning" pin is subsumed by "a well-formed override is in force and locks the key with 409".

#### ①-a The deliberate correction: `.changeset/24882-settings-format-warning.md`, every sentence, read at the merge base

- D0 (front matter) `'@objectstack/service-settings': patch` — falsified: the diff ships a BREAKING narrowing, `minor` under the launch-window convention.
- D1 "feat(service-settings): a settings value that misses the format its `email`, `url`, `phone` or `color` type declares is now reported in the server log; the save is still accepted (#24882)" — falsified: the save is refused with `400`, and the save door writes no log line.
- D2 "Clause-②: no (warning only: every save and every `OS_*` override accepted before is still accepted, with the same value stored or served, the same status and the same errors)" — falsified: the arm is now `(narrowing)`; a save or an override that misses its format is refused.
- D3 "ADR-0007 declares a format for four specifier types: `email`, `url` and `phone` take "format validation", and `color` takes a hex string." — still true; carried verbatim into the new note.
- D4 "Until now nothing judged that format." — still true as history; carried as "Until now nothing enforced it.", which is the exact reading now that PR #25001 judged without enforcing.
- D5 "`PUT /api/settings/branding` stored a Logo URL of `not a url` and answered 200, and an `OS_*` override was served unchecked." — still true as history; carried ("…answered `200`, and an `OS_*` override was served whatever it held").
- D6 "Both doors now judge the format through one shared check, and report a miss instead of refusing it:" — first half still true (`firstFormatMiss` is the one judge), second half falsified; carried corrected as "Both doors now judge the format through one shared check, after every other declared constraint, and refuse a value that misses it."
- D7 "**Save.** When a save is accepted and a key it touches holds a value that misses its type's format, the service logs one `warn` line for that key." — falsified: the save is refused and the `warn` loop is deleted.
- D8 "The line names the setting, the type, the expected format and the value's length." — falsified for the save door: no line exists; the expected format now travels in the `FieldError` message to the caller, who holds the value.
- D9 "**Environment override.** An in-force `OS_*` override whose value misses the format draws one `warn` line, at boot or on the first read." — falsified: the override is not in force and the line is at `error`. The timing clause (boot via `auditEnvOverrides`, else first read) stays true and is restated in the PR body; the new note says "one `error` line per variable and value" without the timing. A remark, not a lost sentence: the sentence as a unit is falsified.
- D10 "The line names the variable, the setting, the type and the expected format." — still true of the new `error` line; carried verbatim.
- D11 "The override stays in force, is served with source `env`, and still locks the key." — falsified; the new note states the opposite.
- D12 "**The value is never printed** in either line, for any key." — still true in substance: the env line never prints the value, the save door has no line and its `FieldError` never echoes; carried as "never the value" and "never echoes the value".
- D13 "The formats are the platform's existing grammars for the same words:" — still true; carried verbatim.
- D14 "`email`: an address with a dotted domain, the grammar the mail transport sends with." — still true (regex unchanged); carried verbatim with an added example.
- D15 "`url`: `scheme://…`, a root-relative `/path`, a `data:` URI or a `blob:` URL." — still true; carried verbatim.
- D16 "An http(s)-only grammar would flag a relative logo path that the branding reader serves." — still true (the root-relative alternative is in the grammar); carried reworded as "A relative logo path that the branding reader serves is accepted."
- D17 "`phone`: digits, spaces and `+ ( ) - .`, at least five characters." — still true; carried verbatim.
- D18 "`color`: `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`." — still true; carried verbatim.
- D19 "Empty values and non-string values are not judged." — still true (`firstFormatMiss`); carried verbatim.
- D20 "Surrounding whitespace is ignored, because the readers trim it before use." — still true; carried verbatim.
- D21 "**Unchanged.** Status codes, response bodies, stored values, the `FieldError`s a refused save carries, and which overrides are in force." — falsified: all five change.
- D22 "Under the standing rule 「甲」, refusing these values waits for the next major version." — falsified by the maintainer's amendment (comment 6303865025 on #6015) and by this diff.

Result: every still-true sentence (D3, D4, D5, the first half of D6, D10, D12 to D20) is carried into the new note. No still-true sentence is lost. No release consumed the deleted note: `@objectstack/service-settings` is at `18.0.0` on main, its `CHANGELOG.md` has no entry for it, and the file was still present in `.changeset/` at the merge base.

#### ①-b The new note: `.changeset/24882-settings-format-refusal.md`, every sentence, against the diff

- N0 (front matter) `'@objectstack/service-settings': minor` — right (② below).
- N1 "fix(service-settings)!: a settings value that misses the format its `email`, `url`, `phone` or `color` type declares is refused, both when it is saved and when it arrives as an `OS_*` override (#24882)" — true (J1, J4).
- N2 "ADR-0007 declares a format for four specifier types: … `color` takes a hex string." — true (D3).
- N3 "Until now nothing enforced it." — true.
- N4 "`PUT /api/settings/branding` stored a Logo URL of `not a url` and answered `200`, and an `OS_*` override was served whatever it held." — true of main.
- N5 "Both doors now judge the format through one shared check, after every other declared constraint, and refuse a value that misses it." — true (J2).
- N6 the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line — right (②).
- N7 the adr-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: "No metadata moves: no spec key, authorable spelling, object definition or stored shape is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, and no exported declaration is removed or narrowed, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite." — true (J8, no spec path in the diff). "What changes is which runtime values two settings doors accept: a value saved through `PUT /api/settings/:namespace` or `setMany`, and a deployment's `OS_*` environment override." — true. "Settings values are runtime state in `sys_setting` (ADR-0007) and environment values belong to the deployment, and no metadata conversion reaches either; a row already stored is not rewritten and is still served." — true (J3). "The remedy is to supply a well-formed value, never a rewrite of a metadata source." — true. "The other categories are closed on facts: the package publishes (not unpublished); no ADR-0087 id is named or touched (not registered or already-registered); and nothing exported is removed or narrowed (not runtime-interface-only, type-surface-only or runtime-export-retired)." — consistent with the tree; the gate accepted the exemption (a notice annotation on the `Check Changeset` run).
- N8 "**BREAKING** (the settings doors' accept set narrows), shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention for breaking changes." — true.
- N9 "The formats are the platform's existing grammars for the same words:" — true (J9).
- N10 "`email`: an address with a dotted domain, the grammar the mail transport sends with. `no-reply@localhost` misses it." — true: the regex requires a dotted domain.
- N11 "`url`: `scheme://…`, a root-relative `/path`, a `data:` URI or a `blob:` URL. A relative logo path that the branding reader serves is accepted." — true for a root-relative path, the spelling the sentence before it names; a document-relative spelling without a leading slash is refused (J9's precision).
- N12 "`phone`: digits, spaces and `+ ( ) - .`, at least five characters." — true.
- N13 "`color`: `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`." — true.
- N14 "Empty values and non-string values are not judged. Surrounding whitespace is ignored, because the readers trim it before use." — true (`firstFormatMiss` returns `null` for a non-string or blank value and tests the trimmed string).
- N15 "**Saving, FROM:** a save naming a value that misses its key's format answered `200` and stored the value as written." — true of main.
- N16 "**Saving, TO:** the save answers `400` with `error.code: 'SETTINGS_VALIDATION'` and one entry per such key in `error.details.fields`, carrying `code` `invalid_email`, `invalid_url`, `invalid_phone` or `invalid_format` (for `color`), and `constraint.type`. Nothing in the save is stored. The answer names the expected format and never echoes the value." — true (J1, J5, J6).
- N17 "**Environment override, FROM:** a malformed `OS_*` override was in force: reads served it with source `env`, and it locked the key against saves." — true of main (the deleted pin file held it).
- N18 "**Environment override, TO:** a malformed `OS_*` override is no longer in force. The server logs one `error` line per variable and value, naming the variable, the setting, the type and the expected format, never the value. Reads serve the next layer instead: the stored value when one exists, otherwise the manifest default, with that layer as the source. The key is no longer locked, so it can be saved through Setup." — true (J4, J5).
- N19 "**Unchanged:** a well-formed value saves, and a well-formed override is in force and locks the key. A value that breaks another declared constraint (a length bound, a pattern) is still refused for that constraint. A value stored before this release is still served by every read, and it does not block a save of the namespace's other keys; only a save that writes that key, or a key its `visible` condition reads, judges it. An all-null save (reset) still clears it." — true (J2, J3).
- N20 "**What to do:** fix the value. For an `OS_*` override, set the variable to a well-formed value or unset it and configure the setting in Setup. For a stored value, save a well-formed value for the key, or clear it." — true; it matches the reporter's own Fix sentence and the reset pin.

### ② Semver level

- The committed changeset bumps `@objectstack/service-settings` alone, at `minor`, marked BREAKING, with the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line at the start of a line in both the changeset and the PR body. Right: the diff adds no published declaration and no `packages/spec` surface (the `yes` arm), and it narrows two published accept sets, the save door's and the env door's (J1, J4). Under AGENTS.md rule 3 the `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING, and the package's own `CHANGELOG.md` shows the launch-window convention shipping a BREAKING narrowing as `minor` at 18.0.0, so the level matches what the diff publishes.
- No `skip-changeset` label is on the PR (labels: documentation, size/xl, tests, tooling), and `skip-changeset` would be wrong: a released package changes behaviour.
- The ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the right category: nothing an author can write is removed, renamed or re-shaped, so no FROM to TO rewrite exists to prescribe; the note's "What to do" paragraph is a runtime value fix, not a consumer code rewrite. The gate accepted it on this head (notice annotation on `Check Changeset`).
- The deletion of the pending warning note is the right correction, not a collision: its sentences are falsified or carried (①-a), the replacement is the one 24882 changeset at the head, and the two sibling changesets main gained since the merge base (24773-oauth-form-types, 24986-cbp-master-edit-object-question) do not share the name.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The dev's open question (os-dev report comment 6305731231, options A confirm the replacement / B restore the warning note beside it): answered A.** Every sentence of the deleted note is either falsified by this diff or carried into the new note (①-a), the note was unconsumed (18.0.0, no CHANGELOG entry), and restoring it would publish "the save is still accepted … refusing waits for the next major version" beside "refused" in one release. The landing rules (landing-operations.md, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION lines) make a same-head at-tier PASS record that judges every rewritten sentence the confirmation when the diff also changes code; this record is that confirmation, naming both notes by path. The `Check Changeset` red stays by design and is not a FAIL input here.
- **Deviation: the pending changeset deleted.** Answered with the open question above.
- **Deviation: `reportRejectedEnvOverride` gains an optional `shape` fragment.** Accepted: private method, set only by the format family, and when set the line carries the length for every key (J5). The other families' lines are unchanged and still print a non-secret value; that is main's behaviour, outside this card, and not re-opened here.
- **Deviation: `constraint: { type }` and no `value` member on the save door's `FieldError`.** Accepted (J6): inside the published open `constraint` record, in the convention the other branches use, and the omission of `value` is what keeps the answer echo-free.
- **Deviation: origin/main moved after the pre-PR merge and was not re-merged.** Not a flag: main is four commits past the merge base, none touches `service-settings`, and the two changesets they add do not collide with the 24882 name; the merge group re-tests the merged tree.
- **Deviations on commit trailers, the merge commit's message, the dual-build rebuild and the worktree removal.** Process notes with no contract bearing; nothing to answer.
- **Acceptance note: `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`.** Its statement that `OS_BRANDING_LOGO_URL` / `OS_BRANDING_ACCENT_COLOR` outrank a saved value and lock the field stays true for a well-formed value; it is silent, not false, on a malformed override now being ignored. Outside the card's file surface, and `Flag docs affected by code changes` is green on this head. Not escalated; a docs follow-up is the lane seat's to file.
- **Acceptance note: `RuntimeConfigPlugin`'s host-level `OS_LOGO_URL` / `OS_BRAND_COLOR`.** Answered: a different reader with its own option contract ("absolute or relative URL"), not judged by the settings door and not narrowed by this diff (J9).
- **Out-of-scope findings (carrier none: the grammar spelled in four places, non-string values stored as given, `company.phone` typed `text`).** Stand as noted; no bearing on this verdict.
- **The earlier open question on PR #25001 (log-only loudness).** Superseded: the seat chose log-only (comment 6303850131), and the amended rule moved the refusal into 18.x (comment 6304784014). Closed.
- **Check-runs on the head, read last, at 2026-10-21T01:42Z: 40 runs.** 27 success, among them Build Core, Test Core (5/6), every Lint lane (CI release and engine gates, ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, the three scoped lanes), every Type Check lane, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, the three claim guards and filter. 7 skipped (the two opt-in harnesses, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance). 1 failure: `Check Changeset`, whose annotations name `.changeset/24882-settings-format-warning.md` as present on the merge base and deleted by this PR, with the two-class text; this is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class the gate's own source declares red by design, and the same run carries the ADR-0087 exemption acceptance as a notice. Pending: Test Core (1/6), Test Core (2/6), Test Core (3/6), Test Core (4/6), Test Core (6/6). A pending run is not a FAIL input; the seat re-reads every run before landing, and the designed-red queue conditions (red by design per the gate's source, not run in the merge group, named on the PR with its reason) are the seat's to confirm from that source; the third is met by this record and the PR body's "Pending release note corrected" section.
